ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$ and $\angle BAC=110^\circ$. Let $D$ be a point on $BC$. Connect $AD$ and construct $\angle ADE=35^\circ$, with $DE$ intersecting line segment $AC$ at point $E$. If $AE=DE$, what is the size of $\angle BDA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $AE=DE$,\\
it follows that $\angle DAE=\angle ADE=35^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle C=35^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BDA=\angle DAE+\angle C=35^\circ+35^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the base. Point D is located on the base BC, and AD is connected. Point E is located on side AC, and DE is connected; therefore AD, DE, and AE form the small triangle ADE, and DB and DC are on the same straight line. Reasoning: It is known that AE=DE, so in triangle ADE, the base angles corresponding to equal sides are equal, namely ∠DAE=∠ADE. It is also known that ∠ADE=35°, therefore ∠DAE=35°. Since E is on AC, ray AE is collinear with AC, so ∠DAE is ∠DAC, namely ∠CAD=35°. In triangle ABC, AB=AC, and the vertex angle ∠BAC=110°, so the base angles are equal: ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°−110°)/2=35°. Because D is on BC, ∠ACD=∠ACB=35°. In triangle ACD, ∠CAD=35° and ∠ACD=35°, therefore ∠ADC=180°−35°−35°=110°. Also because DB and DC form a straight line, ∠BDA and ∠ADC are supplementary, so ∠BDA=180°−110°=70°.
